answer_text:
Looking at this problem, I need to interpret the sequence $a_j$ correctly. The notation has a repeated index, so the natural reading is:

$$a_j = \frac{(1+1/j)^{2j}}{e^j}$$

## Step 1: Analyze $(1+1/j)^{2j}$

Using the logarithm:
$$\ln\!\big((1+1/j)^{2j}\big) = 2j\ln(1+1/j)$$

Expanding the log series:
$$2j\ln(1+1/j) = 2j\left(\frac{1}{j} - \frac{1}{2j^2} + \frac{1}{3j^3} - \cdots\right) = 2 - \frac{1}{j} + \frac{2}{3j^2} - \cdots$$

Therefore:
$$(1+1/j)^{2j} = e^{\,2 - 1/j + O(1/j^2)} = e^2\left(1 - \frac{1}{j} + O\!\left(\frac{1}{j^2}\right)\right)$$

## Step 2: Compute $|a_j|^{1/j}$

Since $a_j > 0$ for all $j$:
$$|a_j| = \frac{(1+1/j)^{2j}}{e^j}$$

Taking the natural log and dividing by $j$:
$$\frac{1}{j}\ln|a_j| = \frac{1}{j}\Big[\,2j\ln(1+1/j) - j\,\Big] = \frac{1}{j}\Big[2 - \frac{1}{j} + O\!\left(\frac{1}{j^2}\right) - j\Big]$$

$$= -1 + \frac{2}{j} - \frac{1}{j^2} + O\!\left(\frac{1}{j^3}\right)$$

## Step 3: Take the limit

As $j \to \infty$:
$$\frac{1}{j}\ln|a_j| \;\longrightarrow\; -1$$

Exponentiating:
$$|a_j|^{1/j} = \exp\!\left(\frac{1}{j}\ln|a_j|\right) \;\longrightarrow\; e^{-1} = \frac{1}{e}$$

Since the limit exists (it's not just a limsup), we have:

$$\limsup_{j\to\infty}|a_j|^{1/j} = \frac{1}{e}$$

$$\boxed{\dfrac{1}{e}}$$
